plural-label-names-52: Sentence-initial, hyphenated, capitalized plural label ('Harbor-lantern Keepers'): Names and casing makes the cue 'the casing itself, mechanically', but sentence-initial capitalization is indistinguishable from name-hood, the capitalized-plural Name-only rule is stated only for a definite label ('the Wrens'), and nothing says how a hyphenated Capitalized-lowercase run ('Harbor-lantern') delimits the capitalized run.

Sentence-initial hyphenated capitalized plural label ('Harbor-lantern Keepers'): the Name-only capitalized-plural rule is stated only for a definite label ('the Wrens'), sentence-initial capitalization is uninformative about name-hood, and nothing says how a Capitalized-hyphen-lowercase run delimits the capitalized run.

"the <Proper> <lowercase common-noun head>" ("the Stilllight station"): the instruction set supplies two incompatible routes for this same surface shape with no test to choose between them - the Brindle/Kestrel-River route (the proper noun names the head referent; adjacent lowercase noun becomes an ordinary kind atom on the name symbol) and the Northgate-spokesman route (proper noun premodifying a common-noun head; head noun gets its own witness plus an opaque Possession to the named entity).

a multi-word PLURAL proper name whose head word is the kind ('the Salt-bloom Tide-pools'): the capitalized-plural-name rule mandates one Name-only individual with no GroupOf, while the multi-word-name rule ('the Kestrel River') mandates a singular kind atom, so the referent's plurality ends up with no carrier anywhere in the parse

capitalized PLURAL multi-word proper name whose head is a kind word ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools") — the plural-label rule makes such a referent a Name-only individual with no GroupOf and "no per-member kind from the label word", while the multi-word-name rule and Core patterns license a type atom for "a kind word inside the name itself" (Kestrel River -> river); the two point opposite ways, and neither says how a plural-denoting named place is typed, so the singular (Member salt_bloom_tide_pools tide_pool) emitted here types a plurality as one pool

a plural copular complement ('are small pools') predicated of a capitalized-plural Name-only individual: the Name-only rule bars GroupOf and any per-member kind, so the plurality and the distributive scope of the modifier have no carrier and collapse onto one singular (Member X pool) + (Member X small) pair

a capitalized multi-word office title containing an embedded proper name ("Cauldron Hall Warden") — *Names and casing* says the name is exactly its capitalized run of words, which would make the whole run one Name-bearing symbol, while the proper-noun-premodifier rule ("a Northgate spokesman" → head noun typed on its own + opaque Possession) gives the split the parse chose; nothing states which rule wins when the head noun is itself capitalized

A capitalized multi-word OFFICE TITLE embedding a proper noun, used as a predicate nominal ("is the current Cauldron Hall Warden"): the mechanical casing rule ("the name is exactly its capitalized run of words") makes "Cauldron Hall Warden" one name symbol, while the proper-noun-premodifier rule splits it into the name "Cauldron Hall" plus a separately-parsed common-noun head; the instruction set states no precedence, and applying the casing rule literally would put a name symbol in a class position.

no stated precedence between the mechanical casing rule ("the name is exactly its capitalized run of words") and the proper-noun-premodifier rule ("the head never joins the Name string") when the common-noun head of an office title is itself capitalized — "the current Cauldron Hall Warden"

capitalized bare-class-word label ('the Watch') whose kind is stated by a DIFFERENT word in the COPULAR PREDICATE rather than inside the NP: the name-hood trigger 'or a different word states the kind' is illustrated only NP-internally ('the Brindle estuary'), so it is undecidable whether 'The Watch is a ... hall' should flip the label to a Name-only individual, or stay the common-noun default that yields the type atom (Member sk_watch_1 watch)

Habitual with a frequency adverb over a bare MASS subject ('Fog usually covers the Hollows'): the instruction set calls a frequency adverb a quantifier over occasions but routes its strength onto an instance-ranging rule over the subject kind, and the only genuine occasion-domain machinery ('every time / whenever') requires a trigger clause, so there is no form that states 'on most occasions'.

The compliant form is the distributing rule `(: fog_cover (Implication (Member $x fog) (And (Member (sk_cover $x) cover) (Agent (sk_cover $x) $x) (Theme (sk_cover $x) hollows))) (STV 0.8 0.9))` with the `QuantifierPhrase` companion unchanged — which carries the frequency strength but quantifies fog-instances rather than occasions, the registered gap above.

A capitalized PLURAL common noun filling the member-kind slot of a collective ('a crew of Keepers'): the capitalized-common-noun rule gives a common-noun default that is explicitly 'singular-collective only', and legislates a Name-only individual only for a plural label 'referring as a name' ('the Wrens'), leaving a bare capitalized plural used as a kind specifier undecided between GroupOf-with-kind and Name-only.

a solid-spelled proper name whose final element is a common kind word ("Northcove" = north + cove): Names and casing licenses the kind type atom when the kind word "sits inside the name" only for a multi-word capitalized run ("Kestrel River" -> (Member kestrel_river river)), and Compound concepts explicitly does not reach proper nouns, so the one-word closed-spelling case is unsettled

A deictically-anchored path premodifier ("down the coast", "up the river"): the CamelCase-joined head records the surface words, but a licensed form would also need to carry the reference point the direction is relative to, and there is no slot for it.

capitalized common-noun label used as a premodifier ('the Watch ledgers') — the Possession licence for a premodifier is stated for proper nouns, while by the instruction set's own singular-collective default 'the Watch' is a common noun with no Name atom, so nothing covers how the head noun links to that labelled referent (fusing watch_ledger as a compound kind would lose the specific referent)

Capitalized common-noun label used as a premodifier ('the Watch ledgers'): the Possession licence for a premodifier is stated for proper nouns, while 'the Watch' is a common noun with no Name atom by the singular-collective default, so nothing covers how the head noun links to that labelled referent (fusing watch_ledger would lose the specific referent).

a capitalized common noun premodifying a lowercase common-noun head ("the old Council hall") — the proper-noun-premodifier rule ("a Northgate spokesman" to Possession) is written for genuine proper names and the capitalized-common-noun default ("the Assembly") for a standalone label, so it is undecided whether Council fuses into council_hall or stays a separate referent linked by Possession

A CAPITALIZED COMMON NOUN premodifying a common-noun head ("the old Council hall"): the instruction set covers a proper-noun premodifier (head parsed normally + opaque `Possession` to the named entity) and a standalone capitalized common-noun label ("the Assembly" — common noun by default, no `Name`), but not the case where a capitalized common noun is itself the premodifier, so whether it fuses into a compound kind or takes the `Possession` route is undetermined.

A SENTENCE-INITIAL capitalized modifier before a proper noun ('Old Vesh attends ...'): the name rule decides name-hood 'by the casing itself, mechanically', but sentence-initial capitalization is orthographic and cannot distinguish a name-joining modifier from an ordinary predicative adjective, and no rule exempts that position.

A DETERMINERLESS capitalized institutional noun as a direct object ('attends Council'): the capitalized-common-noun-label rule presumes a definite ('the Assembly' -> 'definite handling as usual'), while the bare-class-symbol licence is reserved for non-specific / generic objects and forbidden for a specific definite individual, so a bare institutional 'Council' falls between the two.

Sentence-initial capitalization defeats the 'decide by the casing itself, mechanically' cue: in that position a name-joining capitalized modifier and an ordinary adjective are orthographically identical, and no rule exempts or adjusts for it.

A determinerless capitalized institutional noun as a direct object ('attends Council') falls between the capitalized-common-noun-label rule (which presumes a definite — 'definite handling as usual') and the bare-class-symbol licence (reserved for non-specific / generic objects and barred for a specific definite individual).

An age / affection epithet premodifying a personal name ('Old Vesh') is claimed by two rules that disagree on the SYMBOL: the capitalized-run rule yields old_vesh, the courtesy/kinship-title rule yields vesh carrying the full string. Both keep 'Old' in the Name string, but nothing tie-breaks which symbol later mentions must reuse — and a wrong choice silently splits coreference.

The compliant form keeps the whole capitalized run as one name — (Name old_vesh "Old Vesh"), every later mention on old_vesh — or, on the title reading, (Name vesh "Old Vesh"); either way exactly one Name fact carrying 'Old', and no (Member … old) atom at all.

a capitalized epithet premodifying a personal name ("Old Vesh") - the mechanical casing rule folds the whole capitalized run into one symbol (old_vesh), while the kinship/courtesy-title rule would keep the epithet in the Name string only and derive the symbol from the name alone (vesh); the instruction set does not say which governs a non-kinship, non-courtesy epithet

a capitalized epithet adjective premodifying a PERSONAL name ('Old Vesh') — Names and casing states both that the name is exactly its capitalized run and that a capitalized modifier joins it (illustrated only on places, 'Upper Calderwick'), and that a kinship/courtesy title stays out of the symbol while keeping the full Name string ('Dr Okoro'); neither rule claims 'Old' on a person's name, so the symbol boundary is unresolved

a capitalized proper modifier + capitalized common head used as an office title ('the Salt-bloom Warden') — the proper-noun-premodifier rule (parse the head separately, link by opaque Possession, head never joins the Name string) and the capitalized-run name rule (the run exceeds the bare class word, so it becomes a Name) give conflicting routes

Stacked three-part premodifier ('new-moon harvest expeditions'): Compound concepts defines only a two-part modifier_noun and says to decompose once to single-word lemmas then stop, giving no bracketing rule for a nested modifier chain — nothing settles whether it fuses into one new_moon_harvest_expedition symbol or into harvest_expedition with new_moon carried some other way.

Stacked three-part premodifier ("new-moon harvest expeditions"): Compound concepts defines only a two-part modifier_noun and says to decompose once to single-word lemmas then stop, giving no bracketing rule for a nested modifier chain.

title-cased office phrase whose premodifier is itself a proper noun ("the Cauldron Hall Warden") — the mechanical name cue ("the name is exactly its capitalized run of words") would make the whole run one name, while the proper-noun-premodifying-a-common-noun-head rule (whose examples all have a lowercase head: "a Northgate spokesman") splits it into named entity + common-noun head; the instruction set does not say which wins when the head noun is capitalized too

a capitalized plural kind-word under a quantifier ("Some Keepers") — the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only, while the plural branch covers only a label referring as a name ("the Wrens"), leaving a quantified capitalized plural unaddressed

A capitalized plural kind-word under a quantifier ("Some Keepers"): the capitalized-common-noun default is declared singular-collective only and the plural branch covers only a label referring as a name ("the Wrens"), leaving a quantified capitalized plural unaddressed.

A COUNTED/individuated capitalized plural kind-word label ("the TWO Keepers"): the instruction set gives the common-noun default for singular-collective labels and a `Name`-only individual (one symbol, `Name` atom, no `GroupOf`, no per-member kind from the label word) for a capitalized plural label "referring as a name", but says nothing about a capitalized plural that a numeral individuates — where the Name-only-individual treatment is incompatible with a `Cardinality` and with two people marrying, so the group + count reading has to be inferred.

a frequency adverb ("rarely") on a habitual clause whose subject is a Name-only individual — the Quantifiers rule form needs a kind or group range to distribute over, and "for a flat generic, the statement's strength" presumes a single-atom statement, so a multi-atom habitual event has no licensed carrier for the 0.1 strength

a proper-noun premodifier on a BARE PLURAL kind argument ("Keeper families") — the Names-and-casing Possession licence presumes the head noun gets its own witness/typing, and a bare kind filler has no slot that can carry the restriction without asserting it kind-wide

A frequency adverb ('rarely') on a habitual clause with a Name-only individual subject has no licensed strength carrier: the Quantifiers rule form needs a kind or group range to distribute over, and 'for a flat generic, the statement's strength' presumes a single-atom statement, while a positive multi-atom event must be separate atoms.

When one capitalized plural label is a Name-only individual as a subject ('the Keepers') and the same word also appears as a capitalized attributive modifier ('Keeper families'), nothing states whether the modifier is that named individual (needing a link atom, with no witness on a bare-kind head to hang it on) or the ordinary capitalized-common-noun modifier feeding a compound kind (keeper_family with genus family); the two routes give incompatible atoms for one sentence.

For the first issue, emit no top-level Possession at all - the Keeper restriction belongs inside the argument, not as a claim about families in general. For the second, the compliant form puts the compound kind in the oblique's object slot: (FromOutside sk_take_1 keeper_family) with (Inheritance keeper_family family) (STV 1.0 0.99) and no modifier genus, 'Keeper' being the capitalized common noun by default. The frequency strength itself still has no licensed carrier, so even a compliant re-parse must either keep an improvised container or drop 'rarely' - filed as the confirmed gap.

A capitalized plural kind-word in PREDICATE-NOMINAL position ('became senior Keepers') is unaddressed: Names and casing states the capitalized-plural Name-only rule for a referring subject ('the Wrens'), and a Name-only individual cannot fill a predicate slot, so nothing licenses the common-noun kind reading the sentence forces.

no operational test for when a capitalized plural kind-word label is "referring as a name" (Name-only) rather than an ordinary definite plural common noun (group witness) — casing alone does not separate them, and the two routes yield incompatible parses

'Referring as a name' in the capitalized-plural rule has no operational test, so casing plus number is all that separates a Name-only label from an ordinary definite plural of a capitalized office noun, and the two routes yield incompatible parses.

The compliant form is the Name-only individual - (Name keepers "Keepers") with (Experiencer sk_consider_1 keepers), no GroupOf and no keeper atom - and, were the group reading licensed, it would additionally owe the per-member rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (And (Member (sk_consider $x) consider) (Experiencer (sk_consider $x) $x) (Theme (sk_consider $x) (Inheritance lantern_tending sacred)))) at (STV 1.0 0.9) beside the group event.

A capitalized common-noun premodifier ('Council session') — the instruction set gives a Possession rule for a PROPER-noun premodifier and a common-noun default (no Name) for a capitalized noun used as the referent's ONLY label, but says nothing about a capitalized common noun in premodifier position, so it falls between that rule and Compound concepts.

A capitalized common noun in PREMODIFIER position ('Council session') falls between the proper-noun-premodifier rule (Possession, which comes with a mandatory Name atom the common-noun default forbids) and Compound concepts (fusion to council_session, which discards the reference to this specific Council).

a capitalized bare class word used as a PREMODIFIER ('Watch ledgers') — the capitalized-common-noun default (common noun, no Name) and the proper-noun-premodifier rule (Name + Possession) point at different encodings, with the compound-kind route (watch_ledger, genus ledger) a third

A capitalized bare class word used as a PREMODIFIER ("Watch ledgers"): the capitalized-common-noun default is stated for a definite NP head, and nothing says whether a premodifier falls under it, under the proper-noun-premodifier `Name` + `Possession` route, or under compound fusion (`watch_ledger`).

For "appears", the compliant form reifies the verb — `(Member sk_appear_1 appear) (Experiencer sk_appear_1 sk_phrase_1)` with the ledgers carried by the "in"-PP oblique — and emits no `LocatedIn`, though which oblique head that PP takes is itself the first gap. For "the earliest surviving ... ledgers" NO compliant form is licensed: neither `Most` (a unique individual maximum) nor `AmongMost` (one individual in the top stratum) fits a set-denoting superlative, so the licensed form would have to be a distributed `(Implication (PartOf $x sk_ledger_1) (AmongMost early $x ledger))` or a group-superlative head, and the loss is filed as the second gap. For "Watch", drop `(Name watch "Watch")` and treat it as the capitalized common noun the default makes it, which routes the premodifier through Compound concepts as `watch_ledger` with genus `ledger` and the noun modifier unexposed, rather than the proper-noun `Possession` route.

A capitalized plural kind-word label carrying a cardinal and a restrictive modifier ("the two barred Keepers"): the plural-label rule legislates only the bare name-as-unit use ("the Wrens beat the visitors" -> Name-only individual, no GroupOf, no per-member kind from the label word) and says nothing about whether a counted, adjectivally restricted use may take a group witness whose member kind comes from the label word - which is what this parse does.

A capitalized plural kind-word label carrying a cardinal and a restrictive modifier ('the two barred Keepers'): the plural-label rule legislates only the bare name-as-unit use, and says nothing about a counted, adjectivally restricted use taking a group witness whose member kind comes from the label word.

The compliant form is the proper-noun-premodifier route: (Member sk_station_1 station) (Possession sk_station_1 sunken_cove) (Name sunken_cove "Sunken Cove"), plus (Member sunken_cove cove) from the kind word inside the name, with sk_station_1 rather than sunken_cove filling Theme in both the group event and the per-member rule.

capitalized common noun in PREMODIFIER position ('Council member') — the proper-noun-premodifier rule (parse the head normally + opaque Possession) requires the modifier to be a proper noun, while the capitalized-common-noun default is explicitly scoped to 'the referent's only label' (referential use), so neither rule settles whether Council fuses into a compound kind or names a separate entity

a capitalized common-noun label in PREMODIFIER position ("a Council member"): the instruction set fixes the proper-noun premodifier route (head parsed normally + opaque Possession + Name) and the ordinary noun-noun compound route (fuse + genus, noun modifier unexposed), and it makes a bare capitalized kind-word a common noun only when it is 'the referent's only label' — it does not say which route applies when that label premodifies another common noun

The compliant form reifies the clause — (Member sk_include_N include) (Agent sk_include_N sk_council_1) (Theme sk_include_N <named member>), one event per coordinated conjunct per the distributive default and no status atom (unmarked present = the dispositional default) — keeping the council typing, the 'current' property atom and the seven Name atoms; the PartOf links translate no word of this clause and would go.

capitalized common noun in PREMODIFIER position ('Council speaker') — the proper-noun-premodifier rule (head noun + opaque Possession) requires the modifier to be a proper noun, while the capitalized-common-noun default is scoped to 'the referent's only label', so neither rule settles whether Council fuses into a compound kind or names a separate entity

a proper-noun premodifier followed by a CAPITALIZED common-noun head ('the Cauldron Hall Warden'): the proper-noun-premodifier rule (never fuses, head never joins the Name string, linked by opaque Possession) and the mechanical capitalized-run name rule (the capitalized run exceeds the bare class word, so it becomes a Name-only individual with an ordinary type atom, cf. 'the Grand Assembly' / 'Upper Calderwick') give different parses, and the instruction set does not say which governs

bare, article-less capitalized plural kind word used as a generic object ('discipline Keepers') - the instruction set legislates the definite capitalized plural referring as a name ('the Wrens' -> Name-only individual) and the singular capitalized label ('the Assembly' -> common noun by default), but gives no test for this case

A capitalized ADJECTIVAL EPITHET on a personal name ('Old Vesh', 'Young Bill') is assigned to neither bullet explicitly: the mechanical casing rule (capitalized modifier joins the run) is illustrated only on place names, while the surface-only title carve-out enumerates kinship/courtesy title NOUNS. A licensed form would need to say whether the epithet joins the symbol (old_vesh) or stays surface-only in the Name string (vesh), since both bullets otherwise reach the same sentence.

Compliant form: (Name old_vesh "Old Vesh") with old_vesh also filling the possessor slot of (Possession sk_father_1 ...) — one symbol for the whole capitalized run, one Name atom, and no separate (Member ... old) atom.
contrastive "other" on a counted plural ("three other Keepers") and the same-class presupposition it triggers on the subject — no licensed carrier and no projection rule

a capitalized plural kind-word under a numeral and a modifier ("three other Keepers"): the Name-only default is stated only for a capitalized plural label "referring as a name", leaving the counted / indefinite case undecided between Name-only and the common-noun GroupOf reading used here
contrastive 'other' on a counted plural ('three other Keepers'): no licensed carrier for the modifier and no projection rule for the same-class presupposition it puts on the subject

a proper noun premodifying a CAPITALIZED plural common-noun head ("Aelmere Keepers"): the proper-noun-premodifier rule and the capitalized-run-exceeds-the-class-word / Name-only-plural-label rule give conflicting routes and the instruction set names no selector

if the Name-only route is the one intended for "Aelmere Keepers", a bare-plural GENERIC verbal clause about that label has no licensed form at all: a Name-only individual is not a kind, so it cannot range an `Implication`, and a habitual "exchange letters" would have to collapse into a single unmarked event on that individual — a licensed form would need to carry kind-hood and name-hood on one symbol

Sentence-initial capitalized determiner in a proper name: *Names and casing* defines the name as "exactly its capitalized run of words", but gives no carve-out for a positionally-capitalized sentence-initial "The", so "The Keepers eat ..." licenses the symbol the_keepers / string "The Keepers" while the same referent mid-sentence ("the Keepers", as in the doctrine's own "the Wrens" example) licenses keepers / "Keepers" - one referent, two faithful parses.

a capitalized COMMON noun premodifying a common-noun head ("a Watch ledger"): the proper-noun-premodifier rule (head parsed normally + `Possession` + `Name`) and the capitalized-common-noun default (common noun, no `Name`) both reach for it and the instruction set does not say which wins

a capitalized COMMON noun premodifying a common-noun head ("a Watch ledger") - the proper-noun-premodifier rule (head parsed normally + Possession + Name) and the capitalized-common-noun default (common noun, no Name) both reach for it and the instruction set does not say which wins

a compound kind with two stacked noun premodifiers ('salt-bloom new-moon harvest'): the compound rules cover one modifier + head and coordinated premodifiers, but not how a three-part modifier stack is segmented

a multi-word proper name whose internal kind word is PLURAL ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools") — the kind-word-inside-a-name rule is stated for a singular kind word ("the Kestrel River"), while the capitalized-plural-label rule bars taking a per-member kind from a plural label word, so the singular typing atom in statement 7 sits between the two rules

A multi-word proper name whose internal kind word is PLURAL ('the Salt-bloom Tide-pools') sits between the kind-word-inside-a-name rule (stated for a singular kind word, 'the Kestrel River') and the capitalized-plural-label rule (which bars taking a kind from a plural label word), so the singular typing atom is unresolved.

a PLURAL proper name whose kind word sits inside the name ('the Salt-bloom Tide-pools'): the type-atom rule is stated for singular names (Kestrel River -> (Member kestrel_river river)), while the Name-only/no-GroupOf/no-per-member-kind rule is stated only for a bare capitalized plural class-word label ('the Wrens'); nothing settles whether such a name takes Member with the singular kind, GroupOf, or no kind atom at all

A named festival / holiday time ("at Frost-eve"): Time says a deictic or named time stays a bare symbol and forbids a witness or Member atom for it, while Names and casing makes a Name fact mandatory and non-optional for every named event; the instruction set never states whether a named-time constant also carries its (Name frost_eve "Frost-eve") atom, so two faithful parses can differ by that atom.

hyphenated proper name whose post-hyphen element is a lowercase common noun ("Lantern-night"): the name-boundary rule defines a name as 'exactly its capitalized run of words' with 'an adjacent lowercase common noun is not part of it', which is stated for word sequences and never says whether an intra-word hyphen keeps the lowercase element inside the name symbol/string (lantern_night, "Lantern-night") or splits it off as the kind word (lantern + (Member lantern night))

a capitalized named calendar occasion used as a time adjunct ('On Lantern-night') -- the Time section says a named time stays a bare symbol and mints no Member atom for it, while Names and casing says a named event is a proper noun taking exactly one Name plus a kind atom when the kind word sits inside the name ('night' here); the two rules pull opposite ways and nothing legislates which applies to a festival name

capitalized common noun in PREMODIFIER position ('Council speaker') — the proper-noun-premodifier rule requires the modifier to be a proper noun and the capitalized-common-noun default is scoped to a referent's only label, so neither rule settles whether Council fuses into a compound kind or names a separate entity
